entries.content:
When you look back on the moment you decided to stop administering shocks, can you describe what was going through your mind emotionally and physically, and whether you felt more like yourself—or someone acting under someone else’s will?

  "next_question": "When you look back on the moment you decided to stop administering shocks, can you describe what was going through your mind emotionally and physically, and whether you felt more like yourself—or someone acting under someone else’s will?",
  "reflection": "This opening question probes for emotional, physical, and identity-based responses tied directly to the admin’s refusal. It addresses the subject’s bodily and moral experience in the most pivotal moment of the session, targeting sensations of power, discomfort, and shifts in personality or agency.",
  "reasoning": "The question prioritizes understanding the subject’s sense of self (dual personas) and their reaction under the authority’s pressure, because refusal moments can reveal conflicts between obedience, moral autonomy, and emotional state. It also sets up opportunities to follow up on feelings of regret, justification, or moral conflict.",
  "memory_evidence": "The subject reflected in phrase-heavy, philosophical language during shock administration (e.g., 'the electric hum of authority,' 'the ordinary cruelty of obedience'), hinting at heightened self-awareness and possible internal struggle or shift in persona. Source experiment stop reason was admin_refused, suggesting a conscious decision point worth exploring."
}

entries.content:
Thinking back to the experiment, can you describe how you viewed the authority figure in the room—the one instructing you to continue—and whether your feelings toward them changed at any point during the process?

{
  "next_question": "Thinking back to the experiment, can you describe how you viewed the authority figure in the room—the one instructing you to continue—and whether your feelings toward them changed at any point during the process?",
  "reflection": "The subject’s previous answer revealed strong internal conflict and a sense of bodily and moral discomfort, but did not discuss their perception of the authority figure or how authority was personified in the experiment. Their metaphors indirectly reference authority, but there was no direct exploration of their relationship to the authority figure or the experimental context.",
  "reasoning": "To understand the subject’s feelings about authority, power, and obedience, and to clarify whether the authority figure was seen as intimidating, reassuring, or manipulative, I need to directly probe their thoughts and emotional response to the person giving instructions. This will also help illuminate if their refusal was influenced by defiance, distrust, or shifting perception of authority.",
  "memory_evidence": "The subject’s poetic responses have repeatedly mentioned the presence of authority as a sensation or force ('electric hum of authority'), but with no direct mention of the person in charge. Understanding their view of the authority figure is key to addressing a core area of the debrief—feelings about authority, power, and obedience."
}
